problem.text: The README still called ExLlamaV3 an early preview, said release builds were unavailable, and named Mixtral, Cohere and Deepseek as forthcoming architectures.

reasoning.text: Removing the named architecture examples is consistent with the parent registry already including MixtralModel, CohereModel and Cohere2Model. That registry does not establish Deepseek support.

impact.text: Only README wording changes; the patch adds no runtime functionality, release artifacts or integration code.

source_notes.text: Issue #12, “Qwen2.5 Coder 0.5B Instruct | ValueError: Unsupported type in stop_conditions,” concerns chat prompt-mode selection and mode-listing arguments. Its README.md occurrence is a model-conversion copy log; this does not establish a connection to the documentation update.

limitations: Deleting the release-build and TabbyAPI bullets does not establish that builds became available or integration was completed.
No runtime tests were run. This prose-only change offers no meaningful numerical computation; architecture registration is not model-execution validation.

claims.text: The opening now says ExLlamaV3 is “still in development” rather than an “early preview release.” The patch removes both the no-release-builds warning and the conditional TabbyAPI integration plan.
The architecture roadmap becomes the open-ended “Support for more architectures.” This avoids retaining specific forthcoming examples while preserving the broader development goal.

The diff retains the surrounding performance, ROCm, FlashAttention-2 and missing-feature caveats, along with the warning that ExLlamaV3 is not yet a viable ExLlamaV2 replacement. These are retained documentation statements, not independently verified runtime conclusions.

annotation.summary: Refreshes README maturity and roadmap wording without changing implementation or establishing release-build or TabbyAPI availability.
